title: Failure to Rescue
author: Admired Leadership
summary: Borrowing a hospital quality metric, this article explains that 'Failure to Rescue' measures how well healthcare teams recognize and respond to patient complications -- and that the best hospitals distinguish themselves not by avoiding all complications, but by catching and correcting them faster than others. The author extends this framing to leadership: the best leaders aren't the ones who only assemble already-skilled teams, but the ones who actively develop average and struggling performers into strong ones. Citing surgeon-author Atul Gawande's concept of a 'mastery of rescue,' the piece argues this developmental mindset is a harder, more valuable leadership skill than simply talent-picking. It closes asking readers how many average performers they've personally developed into top performers.
